observations: body L1-L3: ATZ = ABZ − BZT and AHZ = ABZ + DZK hold in the plane triangles BZT and BZH, where an exterior angle is the sum of the two opposite interior angles; the bar in L1 (9.7 pt) is a minus sign. By p. 259, L36 ABZ is the angle of latitude, so ATZ and AHZ are corrected angles of latitude, not of longitude, here as in p. 260, L36: al-Battānī's rule (p. 82, L22-L26) takes the variation from the angle of latitude and adds it to the angle of longitude when the corrected zenith distance is the smaller, as for the northern Moon E; (α) and (β) of L8-L9 give the two corrections with ±.

body L1-L10: the figure stands on the right of these lines; it is the figure of p. 259 (L30-L40) cut again, turned about 7° and with flatter vertical circles, and is redrawn from this print: the ecliptic GA, nearly straight; the vertical circles ZT, ZK and ZD, arcs of circles fitted through the apex Z (radius 190.2, 192.5 and 183.9 pt); the circle of latitude EBD and the perpendiculars EL and KD, straight strokes; the stroke from the pole Q to E in eight dashes, the last joined to E. The letters print heavier than on p. 259.
body L4, L17, L19-L20, L24, L29: «Al-Battānī» (L4) has a hyphen (3.5 pt); the long dashes of «al–Battānī» in L17, L20, L24 and L29, of «’l–‘Abbās», «al–Faḍl» and «an–Nayrīzī» measure 4.9 to 5.5 pt.

body L6-L12: in the triangle ZLE, right-angled at L, sin EZL = sin EL : sin ZE, and EZL is BZT, ZT passing through E and ZK through L and B; with sin EL = sin β sin ang. long. : R (p. 259, L40) and ZE = z this is L12, as printed. Al-Battānī's rule (L6) gives the same only for z = 90°. A blot prints above the «(1)» of L12.

body L13-L17: the place is p. 82, L22-L23 («Postea quod e divisione anguli longitudinis provenerat rursus sume et in arcum converte; exibit variatio anguli»); the words in brackets, which Nallino would add, make the rule that of L12. «22–23» has a long dash (5.8 pt); the second o of «oporteret» prints broken.
body L19-L23: «quabus» (L23) is printed for quibus.

body L28-L33: ZBQ and ZEQ, the angles between the vertical and the circle of latitude at B and at the Moon E, are the angles of longitude (p. 259, L36); in the triangle ZEB, sin ZEQ = sin ZEB = sin ZBE sin ZB : sin ZE. A heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition; the dashes of L31 and L32 measure 9.6 pt.
body L36-L37: «EL 2° summum» is the bound of p. 260, L25, which holds for the Moon in the meridian; elsewhere EL is larger (p. 260, L24-L29). The dash before «Ex» measures 10.2 pt.
notes_left L1-L4: Ptolemy puts the arcs β and z for their sines; the β of the formula prints broken.
notes_right L1-L5: the dash before «Schia-» measures 8.4 pt. «Chr )» is printed with a space and no stop. The year 310 of the Hijra ran from 1 May 922 to 20 April 923.
